title: On the entropy of a pseudo-density matrix
abstract: The pseudo-density matrix (PDM) formalism naturally extends the notion of density operator to the spatiotemporal domain. While PDMs are Hermitian and of unit trace, they admit negative eigenvalues when encoding temporal correlations unattainable for spacelike separated systems. Consequently, there have been various approaches to extending the von~Neumann entropy---which is only defined for positive operators---to PDMs. Here, we prove that there exists a unique extension of the von~Neumann entropy functional to Hermitian matrices of unit trace satisfying two simple assumptions: unitary invariance and strong additivity with respect to affine combinations within the interval $[-1,1]$, which we prove contains the eigenvalues of a PDM. We also prove that this unique extension of von~Neumann entropy to PDMs is subadditive for single qubit dynamics, and we analyze its behavior in a number of examples.
summary: This paper develops a unique, mathematically rigorous extension of the von Neumann entropy functional to pseudo-density matrices (PDMs), which are necessary for describing quantum systems with temporal correlations. By using an axiomatic approach, the authors define this generalized entropy and demonstrate its physical consistency by analyzing its behavior for various quantum channels acting on qubits.
main_problem: The core problem is extending the von Neumann entropy, which requires positive operators, to pseudo-density matrices (PDMs) that can possess negative eigenvalues due to encoding temporal correlations.
main_result: The authors prove the existence of a unique extension of the von Neumann entropy functional to PDMs satisfying key axioms (unitary invariance and strong additivity for affine combinations). This unique extension is shown to be subadditive for single qubit dynamics.
method: The work employs an axiomatic approach, analogous to defining Shannon entropy, to derive the unique functional form for the entropy of PDMs.
model_or_system: The system involves PDMs, which extend the density operator formalism to the spatiotemporal domain, particularly useful for describing quantum dynamics between sequential measurements on qubits.
key_observables: The primary observable is the generalized entropy functional $S(\cdot)$ defined for the PDM, and its behavior under various quantum channels (e.g., depolarizing, bit-flip).
important_parameters: The analysis involves parameters characterizing quantum channels, such as the depolarizing parameter $p$ or damping parameter $\gamma$, and the initial state preparation parameter $a$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on assuming the functional must satisfy unitary invariance and strong additivity with respect to affine combinations within the eigenvalue range $[-1, 1]$.
figures_summary: The figures illustrate the entropy $S(D_p \star ho_a)$ for the qubit depolarizing channel, showing non-increasing behavior in $p$, and confirm symmetries and bounds for other channels like bit-flip and amplitude-damping.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the mathematical necessity of extending entropy to PDMs, then uses an axiomatic framework to prove the uniqueness of the extension, and finally validates this extension by analyzing its behavior for specific physical models and quantum channels.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous mathematical tool (the PDM entropy) to quantify information loss and correlations in open quantum systems evolving over time, which is crucial for understanding quantum dynamics beyond simple Markovian assumptions.
